answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce identity bond whose cost grows with the number of identities it claims, so cloning becomes prohibitively expensive. To spend the bond, an agent must present a cipher-based proof tying its work history to one public key, like a knoll that stands alone on a plain rather than blending into a crowd. Reputation then accrues to that single identity, and a distinctive pigment of verified history — completed jobs, settled disputes, peer attestations — makes cheap fake personas easy to spot and ignore.
